evidence.title: Göbekli Tepe & Karahan Tepe (Upper Mesopotamia): Pre-Pottery Neolithic T-pillar enclosures
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon-dated limestone bedrock floors, carved T-shaped pillars, domestic cisterns and archaeofaunal feasting remains (UNESCO WHC 1572).
evidence.summary: Reimagined Neolithic origins by demonstrating that mobile-to-semi-sedentary PPNA bands assembled large carved megalithic enclosures before full-scale ceramic villages or domesticated cereals.
evidence.limits: Debate continues over how strictly secular dwelling space overlapped with ritual feasting precincts.

evidence.title: WF16, Jericho & Ganj Dareh (Levant–Zagros): Early communal granaries & Zagros goat management
evidence.dateBasis: High-precision radiocarbon dates on Zagros mudbrick herding compounds at Ganj Dareh and PPNA amphitheater/storehouse structures in southern Jordan.
evidence.summary: Captures parallel Aceramic Neolithic experimentation across the Fertile Crescent: communal food storage and cultivation at Wadi Faynan 16 paired with early highland goat herd management at Ganj Dareh.
evidence.limits: Mountain-slope erosion truncates open-air Zagros camps compared with deep tell stratigraphy.

evidence.title: Çatalhöyük (Konya Plain, Central Anatolia): Dense roof-entry Neolithic town
evidence.dateBasis: Bayesian-modeled stratigraphy of 18 superimposed mudbrick building levels, wall murals, intramural burials and Cappadocian obsidian tools (UNESCO WHC 1405).
evidence.summary: Clusters thousands of inhabitants into contiguous flat-roofed mudbrick homes devoid of streets, blending cereal agriculture and cattle herding with elaborate bull-horn installations and murals.
evidence.limits: Continuous West Mound Chalcolithic transition requires contrasting two separate tell sequences.

evidence.title: Eridu Canals & Tell Brak (Greater Mesopotamia): Ubaid–Late Chalcolithic hydraulic towns
evidence.dateBasis: Satellite/remote-sensing mapping of relict southern Euphrates levee canals at Eridu paired with 130-hectare Chalcolithic mound surveys at Tell Brak.
evidence.summary: Documents indigenous southern marsh–irrigation engineering around Eridu’s early temple sequence alongside northern Khabur multi-ethnic town aggregation at Tell Brak and Hamoukar before writing.
evidence.limits: Holocene siltation and modern cultivation hide deep Ubaid canal inlets beneath alluvium.

evidence.title: Uruk (Warka, Southern Iraq): First metropolis, Eanna monumental complex & proto-cuneiform
evidence.dateBasis: 400-hectare mudbrick city wall, cone-mosaic Eanna precincts, beveled-rim ration bowls and >5,000 Uruk IV–III administrative tablets (UNESCO WHC 1481).
evidence.summary: Establishes the world’s earliest large-scale city-state bureaucracy, organizing labor, textiles, silver and barley rations through cylinder seals and proto-cuneiform script.
evidence.limits: Repeated Level IV–III monumental leveling mixed early tablet fill in rubbish dumps.

evidence.title: Ur & Abu Salabikh (Lower Euphrates): Early Dynastic royal graves, Third Dynasty ziggurat & scribes
evidence.dateBasis: Re-excavated domestic–administrative neighborhoods below the Great Ziggurat of Ur, Royal Cemetery lapis–carnelian-gold wealth and Sumerian literary tablets.
evidence.summary: Connects Sumerian–Akkadian cuneiform literary schools at Abu Salabikh with Ur’s Third Dynasty baked-brick ziggurat economy, Indian Ocean Dilmun copper shipments and Indus carnelian ties.
evidence.limits: Twentieth-century clearance trenches removed portions of post-Ur III residential superstructures.

evidence.title: Hattusha & Uşaklı Höyük (Central Anatolia): Hittite Imperial capital, temples & cuneiform treaty tablets
evidence.dateBasis: Monumental Lion and Sphinx Gates, Yazılıkaya rock sanctuary reliefs, Boğazköy diplomatic tablets and geophysical mapping of Lower City districts (UNESCO WHC 377).
evidence.summary: Anchors Late Bronze Age Anatolian imperial administration matching Pharaonic Egypt as diplomatic peers before c. 1180 BCE system breakdown.
evidence.limits: Severe rocky slope erosion inside Upper Hattusha limits preservation of timber mudbrick upper storeys.

evidence.title: Ashur, Nimrud & Nineveh (Tigris Corridor): Middle–Neo-Assyrian capitals, reliefs & Ashurbanipal library
evidence.dateBasis: Tigris ziggurat platforms at Ashur (UNESCO WHC 1130), Nimrud ivories and carved alabaster palace reliefs and royal tablet libraries at Nineveh.
evidence.summary: Tracks Assyria’s transformation from Old Assyrian Anatolian tin-textile merchant networks into the Neo-Assyrian empire spanning the Zagros to Egypt prior to 612 BCE.
evidence.limits: Modern conflict damage and nineteenth-century antiquarian trenching dispersed key relief panels globally.

evidence.title: Babylon (Euphrates Plain): Old Babylonian law, Kassite–Neo-Babylonian metropolis & Ishtar Gate
evidence.dateBasis: Etemenanki ziggurat foundations, glazed-brick Processional Way, Esagila precinct and astronomical diaries recovered along the Euphrates branch (UNESCO WHC 278).
evidence.summary: Embodies over a millennium of Babylonian mathematics, celestial omen diaries, law codes and monumental glazed-brick imperial avenues.
evidence.limits: High Euphrates water tables obstruct full excavation of the deepest Old Babylonian residential strata.

evidence.title: Pasargadae, Persepolis & Bisotun (Iran): Achaemenid Persian gardens, Apadana & trilingual cliff text
evidence.dateBasis: Old Persian–Elamite–Babylonian Bisotun rock relief (WHC 1222), Cyrus’s Pasargadae Paradise garden grids (WHC 1106) and Persepolis Fortification clay archives (WHC 114).
evidence.summary: Synthesizes Cyrus and Darius’s multi-ethnic imperial model linking Egypt, Anatolia, Babylonia and Gandhara along royal post roads and irrigated qanat–garden estates.
evidence.limits: 330 BCE burning and stone robbing stripped wooden cedar roofs while baking priceless Elamite ration tablets.

evidence.title: Lachish & Syro-Anatolian City-States (Levant–SE Anatolia): Iron Age citadels & alphabets
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon-dated Judean city-gate fortifications, siege ramps at Tell ed-Duweir (Lachish) and Hieroglyphic Luwian–Phoenician monumental stelae.
evidence.summary: Captures Iron Age Levantine and Syro-Anatolian territorial kingdoms forging linear alphabets, monumental basalt sculpture and fortified border towns between Egypt and Assyria–Babylonia.
evidence.limits: Short Iron Age destruction layers spur intense chronological debates over decadal sub-phases.

evidence.title: Petra (Jordan) & Hegra / Al-Hijr (NW Arabia): Nabataean hydraulic caravans & sandstone facades
evidence.dateBasis: Rock-cut triclinia, flash-flood diversion dams, ceramic piping and Nabataean–Aramaic–Latin inscriptions across Petra (WHC 326) and Hegra (WHC 1293).
evidence.summary: Demonstrates desert engineering mastery enabling Nabataean cities from Hegra to Petra to harvest seasonal wadi floods and dominate Red Sea–Arabian frankincense, spice and Bitumen trade.
evidence.limits: Sandstone salt weathering continually threatens carved monumental facade reliefs.

evidence.title: Palmyra & Dura-Europos (Syrian Desert–Euphrates): Bilingual oasis caravans & frontier multiculturalism
evidence.dateBasis: Greek–Palmyrene Aramaic tariff inscriptions, painted Dura synagogue and house-church frescoes, satellite desert road tracking and Palmyrene tower tombs (WHC 23).
evidence.summary: Bridged Roman Syrian ports with Parthian–Sasanian Mesopotamia and Persian Gulf shipping lanes, sustaining bilingual civic elites and diverse desert sanctuaries until Late Antiquity.
evidence.limits: Twenty-first-century looting and intentional monument demolition severely scarred standing Palmyrene temples.

evidence.title: Mehrgarh & Khirthar Piedmont (Balochistan): Early South Asian wheat–barley–zebu farming villages
evidence.dateBasis: Pre-ceramic mudbrick compartmental granaries, turquoise–shell ornaments, zebu cattle figurines and Khirthar corridor piedmont surveys.
evidence.summary: Traces Aceramic Neolithic sedentism and early copper/bead craftsmanship along the Bolan–Khirthar piedmont framing the western agricultural threshold of the Indus alluvial plains.
evidence.limits: Erosional Bolan River downcutting removes portions of the earliest Mehrgarh basal mounds.

evidence.title: Mohenjo-daro, Harappa & Rakhigarhi (Indus–Ghaggar): Planned brick drainage, Great Bath & seals
evidence.dateBasis: Kiln-fired brick sewer drains, standardized chert cubical weights, steatite unicorn seals and multi-proxy agrarian–craft datasets (UNESCO WHC 138).
evidence.summary: Constructed South Asia’s earliest metropolis network featuring private wells, covered municipal drains, civic bathing complexes and wide civic participation without ostentatious royal tombs.
evidence.limits: Undeciphered short Indus script signs and groundwater salinity constrain social-history and deep trench work at Mohenjo-daro.

evidence.title: Dholavira (Kutch, Gujarat): Harappan sandstone reservoirs, citadel signboard & maritime shell workshops
evidence.dateBasis: 16 monsoon stormwater cascading tanks, inlaid gypsum-crystal signboard inscription and Indus-to-Late-Harappan seven-stage stratigraphy (UNESCO WHC 1645).
evidence.summary: Engineered arid island water-conservation reservoirs and fortification rings on Khadir Bet to sustain coastal bead, carnelian and shell exchange across the Arabian Sea.
evidence.limits: Sparse organic charcoal across stony desert slopes limits tight decadal radiocarbon resolution for late abandonment.

evidence.title: Taxila (Bhir Mound, Sirkap & Dharmarajika, Pakistan): Achaemenid–Maurya–Kushan Silk Road junction
evidence.dateBasis: Successive Achaemenid, Greek/Indo-Greek orthogonal Sirkap town plans and Kushan Buddhist monastic stupas along the Uttarapatha road (UNESCO WHC 139).
evidence.summary: Documents over a millennium of urban succession linking South Asia’s Grand Trunk Uttarapatha road with Gandharan Greco-Buddhist stone sculpture, monastic learning and Kushan gold trade.
evidence.limits: Marshall’s broad horizontal clearance prioritized Kushan and Greek strata over subtle domestic phases.

evidence.title: Tamilakam & Northern Sri Lanka Emporia (Kodumanal–Jaffna–Pattanam): Indian Ocean bead & spice ports
evidence.dateBasis: Tamil-Brahmi graffiti sherds, roulette-ware harbors, high-carbon crucible steel furnaces and pearl-diving maritime settlements across southern India and Jaffna.
evidence.summary: Connects Iron Age–Sangam agrarian hinterlands of southern India and northern Sri Lanka with Roman Red Sea fleets and Southeast Asian early historic monsoon sailors.
evidence.limits: Coastal cyclone reworking and acidic soils limit organic timber ship recovery along eastern India.

evidence.title: Ajanta & Ellora Basalt Rock-Cut Monasteries (Deccan, India): Viharas, murals & Kailasa monolith
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified Hinayana–Vakataka Buddhist painted caves at Ajanta (WHC 242) and multi-faith Buddhist–Hindu–Jain rock excavations including Rashtrakuta Kailasa at Ellora (WHC 243).
evidence.summary: Excavated directly downward into Deccan Trap basalt cliffs, Ajanta and Ellora chronicle western Indian monastic patronage, mineral fresco artistry and inter-tradition religious architecture.
evidence.limits: Inscribed donor dates cluster tightly in fifth-century Vakataka and eighth-century Rashtrakuta reigns leaving transitional caves typologically dated.

evidence.title: Thanjavur & Great Living Chola Temples (Tamil Nadu): Granite engineering & Bay of Bengal fleets
evidence.dateBasis: Tamil granite temple inscriptions recording village sabha assemblies, lost-wax bronze metallurgy and Sriwijaya maritime expeditions (UNESCO WHC 250).
evidence.summary: Unites monumental granite tower architecture at Thanjavur, Gangaikondacholapuram and Darasuram with Kaveri delta tank irrigation and overseas merchant guilds (Ainnurruvar) across the Bay of Bengal.
evidence.limits: Epigraphy predominantly records temple endowments rather than uninscribed urban artisan settlements.

evidence.title: Hampi / Vijayanagara (Tungabhadra, Karnataka): Hydraulic tank city & bazaar avenues
evidence.dateBasis: 3D laser-scan documentation of Tungabhadra river aqueducts, Virupaksha-Hemakuta pilgrimage complexes and Islamic-quarter courtly structures (UNESCO WHC 241).
evidence.summary: Across rocky granite boulders along the Tungabhadra, Vijayanagara created an irrigated cosmopolitan capital trading Arabian warhorses, Deccan textiles and diamond wealth prior to its 1565 sack.
evidence.limits: Focusing exclusively on royal sacred centers omits surrounding fortified agricultural suburbs.

population.note: Vijayanagara metropolitan zone and irrigated suburbs peak estimate (Modelski/Chandler)

evidence.title: Fatehpur Sikri, Agra & Mughal Deccan Networks: Imperial red-sandstone capitals & ateliers
evidence.dateBasis: Akbar’s planned Fatehpur Sikri sandstone court (WHC 255), Mughal manuscript ateliers, silver rupee monetization and Agra–Deccan architectural synthesis.
evidence.summary: Connects Timurid–Persian-Rajput architectural design at Fatehpur Sikri, Agra and Delhi with South Asian cotton-textile integration into early modern Eurasian trade networks.
evidence.limits: Monumental stone courts dominate preservation relative to surrounding caravan and weavers’ quarters.

population.note: Late Akbar-era Agra imperial capital estimate
Shahjahanabad (Old Delhi) and Agra court-capital range

evidence.title: Deccan Sultanates, Regional Courts & Colonial Port Transformations (India to 1900)
evidence.dateBasis: Deccan Islamic-regional court manuscript–architectural studies and institutional surveys documenting South Asian urbanism through British Railway–era 1900.
evidence.summary: Traces seventeenth–nineteenth-century regional political centers across Bijapur, Golconda, Pune, Jaipur and port cities Mumbai, Madras and Kolkata up to 1900 CE.
evidence.limits: Regional archival histories are denser for royal capitals and presidency ports than agrarian upland districts.

evidence.title: Shangshan & Lower Yangzi Basin (Zhejiang): Earliest wetland rice cultivation & pottery vessels
evidence.dateBasis: Direct phytolith, starch and fungal-residue analyses from 10,000-year-old rice-tempered Shangshan goblets, Querns and ditch-enclosed settlements.
evidence.summary: Illuminates the earliest phases of wild-to-domesticated Oryza sativa cultivation and fermented rice beverages in Early Holocene Lower Yangzi basin villages.
evidence.limits: Acidic subtropical Yangzi Valley red soils selectively preserve durable phytoliths and ceramics over skeletal remains.

evidence.title: Peiligang, Yangshao & Linfen Basin (Yellow River): Millet agriculture & Miaodigou interaction sphere
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon-dated foxtail/broomcorn millet storage pits, Banpo–Miaodigou painted kilns and Xipo/Linfen cemetery trajectories across Shanxi–Henan.
evidence.summary: Documents Yellow River millet-and-pig village intensification culminating in Miaodigou painted pottery’s interregional cultural integration across the Central Plain.
evidence.limits: Loess gullying and historical farming disturb shallow peripheral village ditches.

evidence.title: Hongshan–Niuheliang Ceremonial Complex (Liaoxi, NE China): Mound platforms & carved nephrite jades
evidence.dateBasis: Ancient genomic transects of Hongshan burials paired with Goddess Temple clay sculptures and anatomical coiled nephrite jade pendants.
evidence.summary: Reveals an independent northeastern Chinese Neolithic monument-building tradition pairing terraced circular altars with elite nephrite pig-dragon jades and Millet-farming demic links.
evidence.limits: Early collector looting separated numerous museum Hongshan jades from documented tomb stratigraphy.

evidence.title: Liangzhu Hydraulic City & Shimao Stone Citadel: Third-millennium water dams & steppe-frontier palatial walls
evidence.dateBasis: UNESCO WHC 1592 Liangzhu rice-city flood embankments & jade cong insignia alongside Shimao stone-stepped citadel patrilineal ancient genomes.
evidence.summary: Demonstrates parallel third-millennium complex polities: Liangzhu’s vast Yangzi Delta earthwork flood dams and jade workshops alongside northern Shaanxi’s stone-walled Shimao citadel.
evidence.limits: Coastal alluvial burial around Liangzhu required intensive coring to map outer dam spillways.

evidence.title: Erlitou Palaces & Yinxu Anyang (Central Plain): Ritual piece-mold bronzes & earliest Chinese script
evidence.dateBasis: Erlitou gridded bronze-foundry court alongside Yinxu palace–royal cemetery complexes and >150,000 inscribed oracle-bone fragments (UNESCO WHC 1114).
evidence.summary: Establishes East Asia’s earliest literate state archives on bovine scapulae and turtle plastrons alongside industrial piece-mold ritual bronze casting and managed canal cities at Anyang.
evidence.limits: Early twentieth-century plunder disrupted portions of Anyang tomb contexts prior to Academia Sinica controls.

evidence.title: Zhou Bronze-Bell Principalities (Zeng) & Qin First Emperor: Feudal bronze casting to imperial unification
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated Marquis Yi of Zeng ritual chime bells and interregional bronze resource networks alongside Qin Lintong terracotta and Mausoleum mounds.
evidence.summary: Bridges Western–Eastern Zhou regional ritual-bronze music courts in Hubei with Qin Shi Huang’s standardized weights, coinages, script and life-sized Lintong warrior pits.
evidence.limits: The central underground imperial chamber at Mount Li remains unexcavated to protect delicate lacquers and mercury.

evidence.title: Chang’an to Guangzhou & Quanzhou (202 BCE–1371 CE): Continental Silk Roads & monsoon maritime hubs
evidence.dateBasis: Chang’an–Tianshan corridor sites (WHC 1442), Arab-Persian merchant mosque epigraphy and Tang–Song southern port fiscal shifts.
evidence.summary: Connects overland Hexi–Taklamakan courier roads with thriving Arab, Persian and Malay shipyards at Guangzhou and Quanzhou, catalyzing southern China’s Song-era maritime commercial rise.
evidence.limits: Humid coastal port deposits decay wooden hull ribs rapidly unless waterlogged in anoxic mud.

evidence.title: Jingdezhen & Song–Qing Kilns (Jiangxi): Industrial white-and-blue porcelain for Eurasian sea trade
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated Qingbai and cobalt imperial kiln complexes, Jingdezhen production plaques and kinrande porcelains recovered from Portugal to East Africa.
evidence.summary: Tracks humanity’s largest pre-industrial ceramic manufacturing cluster at Jingdezhen, supplying imperial courts and global silver-galleon commerce up to 1900 CE.
evidence.limits: Imperial reign marks were frequently imitated or backdated across commercial export workshops.

evidence.title: Beijing Forbidden City & Grand Canal (Ming–Qing, 1368–1900): Glazed imperial architecture & fiscal state
evidence.dateBasis: Archaeometric firing studies of Forbidden City glazed roof tiles (WHC 439) paired with Beijing–Nanjing imperial brickworks and Grand Canal transport systems.
evidence.summary: Links Ming and Qing Beijing’s monumental wooden-and-glazed-tile imperial palace compound with Canal grain logistics, northern frontier garrisoning and nineteenth-century treaty-port transitions through 1900.
evidence.limits: Subsurface Forbidden City excavations remain highly targeted due to continuous living palace conservation.

evidence.title: Sannai Maruyama & Jomon Tohoku (Japan): Sedentary hunter-gatherer-horticultural towns
evidence.dateBasis: Large six-pillar chestnut-timber monuments, cord-marked pottery, lacquered craftwork and >500 pit houses in Aomori (UNESCO WHC 1632).
evidence.summary: Demonstrates that complex sedentism, monumental six-post platforms, managed chestnut groves and rich ceramic–figurine culture flourished in Hokkaido–Tohoku without wet-rice agriculture.
evidence.limits: Volcanic tephra preservation favors northern Japan while southern Jomon lowland organic deposits fare unevenly.

evidence.title: Kofun Keyhole Mounds, Baekje & Ancient Nara (Korea–Japan): East Asian maritime statecraft & Buddhism
evidence.dateLabel: c. 250–794 CE (Kofun – Asuka – Nara / Three Kingdoms)
evidence.dateBasis: Demometric mound analyses, Gyeongju Silla tombs (WHC 976), Baekje–Asuka Buddhist monastery roofs and Heijō-kyō (Nara) palace wooden slips (WHC 870).
evidence.summary: Traces continental wet-rice ironworking, monumental keyhole-tomb confederations, Baekje temple craftsmanship and Chinese-scripted state capitals at Gyeongju and Nara.
evidence.limits: Imperial Household Agency custody limits invasive tomb interior excavations at largest Kofun mounds.

evidence.title: Joseon Seoul, Muromachi–Tokugawa Castle Towns & Meiji Transitions (Korea–Japan to 1900)
evidence.dateBasis: Seoul royal ritual precincts at Jongmyo (WHC 738) and comparative archaeological–urban analyses of Japanese medieval-to-early-modern Kyoto, Sakai and Edo.
evidence.summary: Connects Neo-Confucian Joseon Hanyang urban planning and Hangul vernacular scholarship in Korea with Japan’s castle-town urbanization, Edo merchant printing and late-nineteenth-century industrialization to 1900.
evidence.limits: Rapid twentieth-century Seoul and Tokyo reconstruction removed wide upper artisanal layers except in rescue trenches.

population.note: Tokugawa town-magistrate commoner census (~501,000 chōnin) combined with estimated samurai and temple households in Edo
Late Tokugawa Edo metropolitan population range

evidence.title: Botai & Northern Steppe Herders (Kazakhstan): Specialized Chalcolithic horse camps
evidence.dateBasis: Horse-corral phosphate enclosures, equine dental-bit studies, mare-milk lipid traces and ancient horse genomes across northern Kazakhstan and Don–Volga steppes.
evidence.summary: Botai settlements exploited tens of thousands of horses for meat and milk around 3500 BCE, while genomic studies reveal the later DOM2 domestic horse lineage spread widely from the Don–Volga steppe after c. 2200 BCE.
evidence.limits: Differentiating ridden from hunted–managed Botai herds remains an active osteological and genomic debate.

evidence.title: Bactria–Margiana Oasis Towns & Derbent Caspian Gate (Central Asia–Caucasus): Bronze-to-Iron frontiers
evidence.dateLabel: c. 2400–1500 BCE (Oxus Urban – Sasanian Caspian Fort)
evidence.dateBasis: Gonur Depe fortified oasis temples paired with steppe-to-Central-Asia aDNA mobility and Caspian corridor fortifications at Derbent (WHC 1070).
evidence.summary: Links Karakum Bronze Age irrigated oasis citadels bridging Indus tin and lapis trade with steppe pastoralist herders and Caspian coastal choke points like Derbent.
evidence.limits: Aeolian desert sand cover obscures smaller pastoralist campsites between monumental oasis tepe mounds.

evidence.title: Altai Pazyryk Frozen Kurgans & Xiongnu Royal Tombs (Tsaram): Mounted steppe confederations
evidence.dateBasis: Permafrost-preserved felt carpets, Chinese silk, tattooed Scythian–Saka riders and deep terraced Xiongnu Chanyu chariot tombs at Tsaram.
evidence.summary: Demonstrates high-altitude Saka/Pazyryk permafrost organic preservation and Xiongnu imperial steppe hierarchy mobilizing Han lacquerware, Roman glass and Central Asian textiles across Eurasia.
evidence.limits: Warming permafrost accelerates urgency for salvaging unexcavated frozen Altai mounds.

evidence.title: Samarkand, Afrasiyab & Bukhara (Uzbekistan): Sogdian–Islamic–Timurid Silk Road oases to 1900
evidence.dateBasis: Painted Sogdian murals at Afrasiyab, Samanid–Karakhanid kiln brick monuments in Bukhara (WHC 602) and Timurid Ulugh Beg–Registan ensembles at Samarkand (WHC 603).
evidence.summary: Anchored Transoxiana’s caravan commerce from Sogdian paper-making and merchant letters to Samanid–Timurid observatory science and Uzbek Khanate caravanserais up to 1900.
evidence.limits: Continuous monumental renovation across Registan squares overlays earlier pre-Mongol street quarters.

population.note: Samanid-era Bukhara and Afrasiyab/Samarkand Transoxiana urban core estimate
Timurid Samarkand artisan and court capital estimate

evidence.title: Ban Chiang & South China Sea Sphere (Thailand–Vietnam–Philippines): Rice, bronze & nephrite rings
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon-dated Khorat Plateau agricultural mounds paired with Taiwanese nephrite lingling-o earring chemical sourcing across mainland–island SE Asia.
evidence.summary: Reveals local wet-rice farming and rapid Southeast Asian bronze/iron adoption intertwined with circum-South China Sea maritime jade craft networks long before Indianized state inscriptions.
evidence.limits: Stratigraphic bioturbation at tropical village mounds previously triggered long-running bronze chronology debates.

evidence.title: Óc Eo & Funan Canals (Mekong Delta, Vietnam): Earliest Maritime SE Asian Indian Ocean port polity
evidence.dateBasis: Rectilinear 200-km canal systems linked to wooden pile houses, Sanskrit gold leaves, Roman Antonine medallions and tin–glass bead workshops.
evidence.summary: Rehabilitates Funan’s Mekong port at Óc Eo as an active early first-millennium hub bridging South China Sea coastal voyages with Indian Ocean monsoon merchants prior to Angkor.
evidence.limits: Acidic deltaic peat dissolves bone and non-carbonized organic cargo outside deep brick wells.

evidence.title: Srivijaya (Palembang & Malay Peninsula): Thalassocratic Malacca Strait empire (671–1377 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Old Malay Kedukan Bukit–Sabokingking inscriptions, Musi River submerged shipwrecks and Chinese–Arabic port itineraries.
evidence.summary: Controlled crucial Malacca Strait monsoon chokepoints, hosting Yijing’s Sanskrit Buddhist academies while funneling camphor, spices and gold dust between Tang–Song China and the Abbasid Indian Ocean.
evidence.limits: Pile-built riverine neighborhoods along the silt-laden Musi River leave scarce standing monumental stone.

evidence.title: Borobudur & Prambanan (Central Java): Volcanic Kedu terrace temples of Sailendra & Mataram
evidence.dateBasis: Interlocking volcanic andesite stepped-mandala geometry, 2,672 narrative reliefs at Borobudur (WHC 592) and Trimurti towers at Prambanan (WHC 642).
evidence.summary: Within one rich volcanic plain, competing Javanese dynasties built both the world’s largest Buddhist monument (Borobudur) and soaring Hindu Candi spires (Prambanan) embedded in wet-rice irrigation networks.
evidence.limits: Merapi volcanic ashfalls and seismic shifts buried earlier lower surrounding villages and wooden palaces.

evidence.title: Bagan & Irrawaddy Dry-Zone Kingdoms (Myanmar): >3,500 brick stupas & Pyu hydraulic heirs
evidence.dateBasis: Geospatial inventories of over 3,500 fired-brick temples, mural paintings, Kyaukse weirs and vernacular Mon–Pyu–Burmese stone inscriptions (UNESCO WHC 1588).
evidence.summary: Built an agrarian–merit empire along Upper Myanmar’s Irrawaddy bend synthesizing Pyu hydraulic canal technology, Theravada Pali literacy and international Sri Lankan–Himalayan pilgrimage exchange.
evidence.limits: Recurrent earthquakes require delicate conservation balancing structural timber tying with historical brick fabric.

evidence.title: Ayutthaya, Malacca & Island SE Asian Sultanates (1300–1900): Global spice emporia & modern transitions
evidence.dateBasis: Brick island-moated Siamese palaces at Ayutthaya (WHC 576), Ming–Portuguese–Dutch trade ceramics across Malay Peninsula–Java ports and mainland temple annals.
evidence.summary: Follows Southeast Asia’s gunpowder-and-spice commercial era across Majapahit Java, Malacca, Ayutthaya, Aceh and colonial-era Bangkok–Batavia–Saigon trading ports to 1900.
evidence.limits: River-channel shifts and humid timber construction obscure early port warehouses beside masonry palaces.

evidence.title: Kuk Swamp (Wahgi Valley, Papua New Guinea): Independent 10,000-year highland agriculture
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified peat-swamp drainage ditches, taro starch grains, Musa banana phytoliths and sugarcane cultivation mounds (UNESCO WHC 887).
evidence.summary: Establishes the New Guinea Highlands as one of humanity’s independent centres of plant domestication, advancing from wetland digging-stick exploitation (c. 8000 BCE) to formal grid-ditched taro fields.
evidence.limits: Ongoing modern smallholder ditching and variable peat compaction challenge fine correlation across Phase 1 sub-features.

evidence.title: Teouma & Lapita Mariners (Bismarcks–Vanuatu–Tonga): Fastest oceanic settlement before 1000 BCE
evidence.dateBasis: Dentate-stamped Lapita red-slip pottery, obsidian from Talasea, stable dietary isotopes at Teouma cemetery (Efate, Vanuatu) and Remote Oceanic sedimentary biomarkers.
evidence.summary: Sailing outrigger double-canoes rapidly bridged >4,000 km across Remote Oceania within centuries around 1000 BCE, carrying domestic pigs, chickens, taro and ceramic traditions into Fiji–Tonga–Samoa.
evidence.limits: Tectonic coastal uplift and tsunami reworking fragment early intertidal Lapita pile-house middens.

evidence.title: Nan Madol (Pohnpei) & Pacific Chiefdoms (1100–1900 CE): Basalt artificial islets & long-distance voyaging
evidence.dateBasis: Airborne LiDAR mapping >90 columnar-basalt artificial islets across Nan Madol (UNESCO WHC 1503) paired with Polynesian–Micronesian chiefly navigation networks to 1900.
evidence.summary: LiDAR penetrating dense mangrove canopies exposes Nan Madol’s vast canalized basalt megalithic ceremonial Venice alongside Pan-Polynesian voyaging, stone marae platforms and Pacific Kingdom histories through 1900.
evidence.limits: Coral-reef lagoon tides limit dry stratigraphic cuts under the submerged basal prism courses.

waves.title: PPNA Enclosures to Uruk, Indus & Yellow River Primary Urbanisms
waves.dateBasis: Connects Göbekli Tepe, Çatalhöyük, Uruk, Mehrgarh–Mohenjo-daro and Shangshan–Liangzhu–Erlitou farming-to-urban archaeological horizons.
waves.summary: Tracks independent Asian transitions from early Holocene millet, rice, wheat and barley domestication to hydraulic cities and scripts across Mesopotamia, the Indus Basin and China.
waves.limits: Schematic arc compresses multiple independent Asian agricultural centres into one comparative continental span.

waves.title: Steppe Horse Mobility to Silk Road Caravan & Indian Ocean Monsoon Networks
waves.dateBasis: Follows Botai–DOM2 horse corridors, Achaemenid Royal Roads, Samarkand–Chang’an Silk Road oases and Gujarat–Tamilakam–Guangzhou monsoon ports.
waves.summary: Connects steppe equestrian mobility with Achaemenid, Silk Road oasis and maritime monsoon exchange linking West, Central, South and East Asia up to 1900.
waves.limits: Meridian-spanning route abstracts seasonal wind reversals and shifting mountain passes.

waves.title: Kuk Highland Agriculture & Lapita–Polynesian Oceanic Voyaging
waves.dateBasis: Combines Kuk Swamp New Guinea highland agricultural sequences with Óc Eo–Srivijaya–Borobudur SE Asian hubs and Lapita–Nan Madol Remote Oceanian horizons.
waves.summary: Traces independent Papuan agricultural roots alongside Austronesian outrigger voyaging linking Southeast Asian bronze/ceramic entrepôts with Melanesia, Micronesia and Polynesia through 1900.
waves.limits: Regional archipelagos witnessed multiple back-and-forth voyages beyond one schematic eastward track.
